translations.text: A copy of the letter that Jeremiah sent to the captives taken to Babylon, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive, to instruct them as he had been commanded by the Lord.
Because of the sins you committed before the Lord, you were taken captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
When you enter Babylon, you will be there for many years, a long time, up to seventy years. After seventy years, I will bring you out of there in peace.
Now look: in Babylon you see gods of silver, gold, wood, and stone, carried on shoulders, which become objects of fear for the nations.
So take care that you too do not become like the nations. Do not fear them or tremble before them.
When you see large crowds in front of them and behind them worshiping them, say instead in your hearts, “You alone, Lord, should be worshiped.”
For the angel of the Lord is with you, and he will look after your lives.
For they have a tongue carved by a carpenter, and they are overlaid with gold and silver, but they cannot speak, because they are worthless and dead.
Just as adornment looks beautiful on a virgin, so they take gold

People forge crowns and place them on the heads of their gods. Yet it is well known that when their priests are enjoying themselves, they remove gold and silver from their gods and spend it on themselves.
They give some of the crafted material to prostitutes, and they adorn them with clothing like human beings—these gods of gold, silver, and wood.
Yet these gods cannot escape tarnish and decay. They are dressed in purple clothing,
and people polish their faces because of the dust that rises onto them from the building.
One holds a staff like a man who judges this region, yet it cannot destroy those who sin against it.
It holds a sword in its right hand and an axe in its left, but it cannot save itself from war or robbers. From these things you should recognize that they are not gods. Do not fear them.
For just as a clay vessel is useless once it is broken,
This is what their gods are like: they are set upright in buildings, and their eyes are full of dust from the dirt on the feet of those who enter and leave.

Like someone condemned by a king, their arms are confined, as though they were condemned to death. Their priests secure their buildings and shut them with bolts and bars so that robbers will not steal them.
They light many lamps for them, though their eyes cannot see.

They are like the beams of houses, and their heart wanders and goes astray. They are ruined by the crawling creatures of the earth; both they and their clothes are eaten away, and they do not know it.
that their faces are sooty and black from the smoke that rises from the building.
On their bodies and on their heads sit bats, swallows, and ravens together, and cats as well.
From these things you will recognize that they are not gods. Do not fear them.
For the gold with which they are overlaid for beauty does not shine unless someone polishes away its tarnish. Even when they were being melted down, they felt nothing.
For they are bought at a high price, yet there is no breath in them.
They are carried on shoulders because they cannot walk, and they display their shame to human beings. Let those who serve them also be ashamed.

For if they fall to the ground, they cannot get up. Even if someone sets them upright, they cannot move. Nor, if one leans over, can it straighten itself. Instead, food is set before them as before the dead.
Their priests eat the sacrifices offered to them, and their wives take their pleasure from them. They give nothing to the poor and needy

from their sacrifices. A woman approaches them during her menstruation, during childbirth, and in her uncleanness. From these things you should know that they are not gods, and you should not fear them.
For how can they be called gods? Look, women prepare these gods of gold, silver, and wood.
In their dwelling places the priests sit with their clothes torn, their heads shaved, their beards clipped, and their shaved heads uncovered.
They howl loudly before their gods, like people at a funeral feast.
The priests take some of their clothing and dress their wives and children in it.
Even if someone does them harm or good, they cannot repay him. Nor can they appoint or remove a king.
Likewise, they cannot give anyone wealth or money. If someone makes a vow to them and does not fulfill it, they will not demand it from him.
They cannot save a person from death or rescue the weak from the strong.
They cannot give sight to a blind man or rescue someone suffering from distress.
They have no mercy on the widow, do no good to orphans, and do not provide for the poor.

The gods of wood, silver, and gold are like stones lying in the mountains. Let those who serve them be ashamed, for they know that there is no usefulness in them, yet they lead people astray through them.
How can they be recognized as gods?

Look, even the Chaldeans treat them with contempt: when they see someone with a speech impediment who cannot speak, they bring him up to the entrance and ask him to speak and call out, as though he could understand.
Yet they themselves cannot understand that they should abandon them, for they have no understanding.
Women adorn themselves with cords and sit along the roads, burning fine incense.
But when one of them is led away by a passerby and sleeps with him, she taunts her companion, saying, “I have not made you my equal.” Nor has her companion’s cord been cut.
Everything done for them is futile. How, then, can people testify that they are gods? Or how can they be called gods?
They were made by the hands of a carpenter and a metalworker, and they are nothing. They were not made as they themselves wished; rather, their craftsmen make them as they wish.
But if their craftsmen themselves do not last very long,
How, then, is it possible for the things they made to be gods? For they have left falsehood and disgrace to those born after them.
For when war and disaster come upon them, their priests deliberate among themselves about where to hide them along with themselves.
How, then, should people not recognize that they are not gods, but the work of human hands? They cannot save themselves from war or from disaster.

For these things made of wood, silver, and gold will eventually be known to all nations as falsehoods. It will be clearly apparent to the king that they are not gods, but the work of human hands, and that none of God’s works are in them.
Look, everyone knows this: they are not gods.
For they cannot establish a king over the earth, nor can they harm or rescue anyone. They cannot give rain to human beings.
They cannot pass judgment, even on their own behalf. Nor can they deliver someone who is wronged from someone stronger than he is, because they are powerless.

Nor do they fly through the air between heaven and earth like ravens. For when fire breaks out in the temples of the gods, their priests flee outside and save themselves, while the gods burn like beams in the midst of it.
They cannot stand against a king or before a warrior.
How, then, can they be recognized or believed to be gods, when these gods of wood, silver, and gold cannot even save themselves from thieves or robbers?
For strong and powerful people take the gold and the clothing that are on them and go away, and not one of them can help itself.
A king who displays courage is better than they are. A useful household utensil that its owner uses is better than false gods. A door that protects its owner is also better than false gods.
The sun, moon, and stars are lights in heaven shining upon the earth. They are sent to perform their tasks, and they obey.
Lightning, too, when it flashes, is very splendid. So also is the wind that blows throughout the whole region.
When the clouds are commanded by God to go and bring rain upon the whole inhabited world, they go and carry out what they are commanded.
Even the fire sent from above to burn mountains, hills, and forests does what it has been commanded. But these gods do not resemble any of these works in appearance, power, or action.
For this reason, how can they be called gods, or thought to be gods, when they cannot even pass judgment, or do good or harm to human beings?
Know, therefore, that they are not gods, and do not fear them.
For they can neither bless a king nor curse him.
They cannot display signs in heaven to the nations. Nor can they make their light rise like the sun, and they do not shine like the moon.
Wild animals are better than they are, because the animals can flee and save themselves.
Nothing shows us that they are gods. Therefore, do not fear them.
For like a shelter in a cucumber patch that guards nothing, so are their gods of wood, silver, and gold. There is no benefit in them.
They are like a scarecrow in a garden on which every bird settles. Their gods of wood, silver, and gold are also like a dead person lying in darkness.
For from the purple cloth and silk upon them, which decay, you will know that they are not gods. They themselves will also ultimately decay forever and become a disgrace in the land.
But it is well with the righteous man who has no idol, who is far from disgrace and waits for the Lord God.
